notes: Source pages explicitly identify these assets as CC0. SHA-256 hashes identify original downloaded files before editing. The authored-* sources are electronic game sounds synthesized in this repository by deterministic scripts and dedicated CC0; they have no download. Reveal-specific excerpts, processing and outputs are listed separately under files. No NASA audio is included.

sources.title: Cat Purr & Meow
sources.author: Kerzoven
sources.notes: Creator-recorded cat vocalizations. The page notes background noise in the meows. Two of the page's files are used: cat_mewpurr.wav (download) and cat_softmew.wav (additionalDownloads; its link, size and CC0 license were checked on the source page on 2026-09-25).

sources.title: Water Waves
sources.author: transitking
sources.notes: OpenGameArt provides a wave excerpt from transitking's recording and identifies it as CC0. Downloaded locally as wave.flac.

sources.title: Swishes Sound Pack
sources.author: artisticdude
sources.notes: Thirteen WAV effects created for Summoning Wars: four lighter and nine heavier swishes. Creator describes recording moving wood and a clothes hanger.

sources.title: 100 CC0 SFX
sources.author: rubberduck
sources.notes: One hundred recorded effects, including paper, bells and wood. The page labels the archive 100-CC0-SFX.zip; the actual download URL includes _0. Downloaded locally as foley.zip.

sources.title: Atmospheric Interaction Sound Pack
sources.author: legoluft
sources.notes: Forty-three WAV effects from krank. OpenGameArt marks them CC0 and links the original project, which identifies its license as Public Domain. Downloaded locally as magic.7z.

sources.title: 40 CC0 water / splash / slime SFX
sources.author: rubberduck
sources.notes: Forty effects: bubbles, water loops, slime and splashes. The creator describes some slime sounds as recorded from real slime. Downloaded locally as bubbles.zip.

sources.title: Rocket Engine
sources.author: theMinesAreShakin
sources.notes: User-selected rocket/spaceship effect described by its creator as a low rumble and tagged loopable. The source page explicitly identifies it as CC0. The original stereo PCM WAV is approximately 6.09 seconds at 48 kHz. This is a game sound effect, not NASA audio.

sources.title: Drum roll 2 L
sources.author: Joseph SARDIN
sources.notes: Snare drum roll created with HALion Sonic SE in Cubase. The creator's page explicitly identifies it as CC0 and permits editing, redistribution and commercial use without attribution. The original MP3 is 5.068 seconds; downloaded locally as confetti-candidates/joseph-sardin-drum-roll-2-l.mp3.

sources.title: Trumpet Fanfare
sources.author: Graciano Choc - Bz.gamedev (gchoc)
sources.notes: Short trumpet fanfare, explicitly licensed CC0 by uploader gchoc; the page's attribution notice names Graciano Choc - Bz.gamedev. The original MP3 is approximately 2.42424 seconds; downloaded locally as confetti-candidates/graciano-choc-trumpet-fanfare.mp3.

sources.title: Tiny creatures sounds (laugh.ogg)
sources.author: fvcalderan
sources.notes: Creator recorded their own voice, pitched it up and added effects in Audacity. The source page explicitly identifies the sounds as CC0. Original laugh.ogg is approximately 1.73004 seconds; downloaded locally as fairy-candidates/fvcalderan-laugh.ogg.

sources.title: Pixel Quest chiptune stems (authored in-repo)
sources.author: Student Grouper contributors
sources.notes: Synthesized in this repository by a deterministic script (numpy; no samples): band-limited pulse waves, a 4-bit stepped triangle and 15-bit LFSR noise playing an original melody. It imitates no famous game melody or trademark sound. Running `python scripts/authored-sounds/pixel-quest.py work/open-sounds` writes the stems to work/open-sounds/authored/pixel-quest/ plus NOTES.json listing every note. The script and its output are dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

sources.title: Block mine game blips (authored in-repo)
sources.author: Student Grouper contributors
sources.notes: Synthesized in this repository by a deterministic script (numpy; no samples): soft mallet-style electronic blips (fast-decaying sine partials plus a short filtered-noise strike) on a stepwise C-major pentatonic, modelled on no existing game's sounds. Running `python scripts/authored-sounds/block-mine.py work/open-sounds` writes the stems to work/open-sounds/authored/block-mine/ plus NOTES.json listing every note. The script and its output are dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.
